C1.why: At 01:57 he never named his fiancée, so Amal's 'عيانة؟' reads as a clarifying question ('she's sick?'). The call then dropped, and he restarted the same sentence at 02:21, where the correction is clear. This is the same moment as C2, and C2 is the better candidate.

C2.why: He said 'خطيبتي شوي عيان', using the masculine adjective for a feminine noun (A8). Amal recast it as عيانة, he repeated 'Yeah, عيانة', and she typed '5atibti shwai 3ayaane' in chat. This is the clearest corrected version of the 01:52–02:26 moment.

C3.why: He said 'هي بيوجع', then added 'راسها' after it. This is not a clean self-fix, because the sentence was still broken. Amal recast it twice ('هي راسها بيوجع' / 'راسها بيوجع'), he repeated it, and she typed 'raasha beywajje3' in chat. Confidence is moderate because a verb-first order like 'بيوجع راسها' can be acceptable.

C4.why: Her 'خلاص؟' only asks 'done?', which is not a correction. He changed تلات to ثنتين himself, and her chat just types up his final answer. This is a self-fix.

C5.why: He asked 'Is it بنقلق?' while working out the meaning. Amal offered the adjective, but she also kept the verb as an option ('Or I worry. Do you wanna say I worry?'), so she did not reject بنقلق. The state word (participle, B15) is also not taught yet.

C6.why: This is the same moment as C5, so it cannot be a second slip. It is also a question about which form to use, not a rejected error.

C7.why: He said قلقان and then قلقانين at 06:52, before Amal's 'إحنا group' at 06:53. That is a self-fix before she reacted.

C8.why: He tried لـ (لا الـ نار / لـ النار) for 'worried about fire'. Amal corrected it: 'Men not', 'You're worried from'. He then switched to من نار. Fixed preposition after قلقان (D2).

C9.why: He guessed يبدأ with a question mark for a word he did not know yet. Amal set it aside and never gave the right word. This is a vocabulary gap, not a corrected mistake.

C10.why: He had just asked how to say 'take care of' (09:10), so the phrase was new. Amal was building it with him piece by piece and had never given على before. His بالـ was cut off, so this is guided teaching of a new phrase, not a corrected slip.

C11.why: At 11:35 he said ديرت بالي خطيبتي without على. At 11:45 Amal named the rule ('على. بدير بالي takes على.') and he fixed it at 11:50. This is D2: the verb picks its own preposition. All three claims describe this one moment.

C12.why: ديري بالِك (baalik) is the correct feminine command when he speaks to Amal. باليك is most likely the speech-to-text engine spelling 'baalik'. Amal first said 'Mm', then only noted that دير بالك is the command form. That is an explanation, not a clear rejection.

C13.why: After خلينا he used the past-tense عملنا. Amal said نعمل right away and he repeated خلينا نعمل. This is B2: after خلينا the next verb is bare present. All three claims describe this one moment.

C14.why: He was searching for a word he had forgotten and asked 'is it عصافير?' as a question. He had already said 'No. That's bird' himself at 16:04. Amal's 'No, birds' answered his question, so it is a word hunt, not a corrected mistake.

C15.why: Amal prompted 'one?' after he said غيم, he changed it to the plural غيوم, and she accepted it with مم. That is prompt-then-fix (A9 plurals). Confidence is lower because غيم can work as a collective noun and he may have started fixing it himself ('مش...') before she spoke.

C16.why: This is the same moment as C15 (غيم to غيوم at 16:46–16:51). One slip per moment, and C15 is the better grammar framing.

C17.why: He repeated her Arabic sentence correctly. His mistake was understanding بتطلع as 'look at' when he put it into English. Amal fixed his understanding, not anything he produced in Arabic.

C18.why: 'Does it have to do with Azan?' was a question while he hunted for the word, and Amal answered it. The سجر claim is the same moment as C19, which covers it better.

C19.why: He said the wrong form سجر for dawn and Amal recast it as فجر. He then checked 'فجر or سجر?' and took فجر, which was taught in an early lesson. This is the one corrected moment for dawn.

C20.why: He said غير لو for 'other than' and Amal clearly cut it: 'No لو. غير.' She then explained that لو belongs in حتى لو. The ق/غ difference is a speech-to-text error and not part of the slip.

C21.why: Medi said غير الشمس (20:03). Amal recast it as غير شمس twice (20:12, 20:30) and said 'نوءل' (no el-). He then used غير شمس at 20:52. This falls under the A16 rule: no el- after غير.

C22.why: 'Is it طيور؟' was Medi asking which word to use, not a wrong form he produced. Amal only asked whether he meant bird or plane. This is word-finding, not a corrected slip.

C23.why: Medi said في الليل سما, with no el- on سما and the night phrase first. Amal recast it as السما بالليل (21:43) and he repeated it. She said بالليل and في الليل are both fine, but the fix to السما stood.

C24.why: Medi first said في قمر, then asked 'القمر؟', which is a tentative question. Amal's 'قمر. قمر.' is not clearly a rejection: her own chat at 24:15 writes 'fi el-2amar', so the definite form is acceptable to her.

C25.why: Medi said نجمة تاني, using the masculine form after a feminine noun. Amal echoed 'تاني.' as a prompt, he changed it to تانية (24:54), and she approved with 'مهم'. That is a prompt-then-fix on gender agreement (A8/A14). All three claims describe this one moment.

C26.why: Medi said بشوف اليوم and left off the pointer ending, even though نجمة had been fronted. Amal prompted him with 'Point it back' (جملة is likely a mishearing of نجمة). He then fixed it to بشوفها and said 'I forgot the pointer rule'. This is a corrected C2 pointer-rule slip.

C27.why: Medi did not know the word for 'since'. He asked about it as questions ('since is لسا, right?', 'Is it لا?'), then asked 'What's since?' and Amal supplied من. This counts as asking for a word he did not know yet, not a mistake in his own Arabic.

C28.why: Medi asked a question ('is the verb بمطر?'), and Amal answered 'بتمطر, yes'. That 'yes' suggests she may have heard him right or did not treat it as an error, so it reads as a question about the form. The speech-to-text may also have misheard him. Leaning not a slip, with low confidence.

C29.why: 'mara-mara-maratat' was a tangled try at saying مطرت. Amal laughed and called it a tongue twister, so she treated it as a pronunciation stumble. Nothing shows a wrong past-tense form; this is a stutter, not a grammar slip.

C30.why: Medi said الأول هون where he meant 'the air here'. Amal recast it as الهوا هون. When he asked what he had said, she confirmed she heard الأول, so it was a real mistake and not a speech-to-text error. Of the 3 claims, the second (wrong الأول, right الهوا) is the best.

C31.why: Medi offered غير من ('different from' with من). Amal corrected it to عن and repeated عن at 32:21. He took the fix: 'غير always takes عن'. He did ask 'right?', but it was his own wrong attempt and she corrected it, so it counts (card A21: غير + عن).

C32.why: Medi said آخر المرة for 'the last time'. Amal named the rule: آخر المرة means 'the end of the time'. She then confirmed آخر مرة (cards A15 / A20).

C33.why: Medi said masculine كان for the feminine subject مرة. Amal prompted 'مرة is...' and he fixed it to 'feminine. كانت.' (B18, the verb matches its subject).

C34.why: Amal asked how to say 'ago', so this was a quiz, not Medi asking for a word. He answered ثلاث سنين الماضي. She said 'No' and gave قبل ثلاث سنين (E6).

C35.why: This is a separate moment from C34. After her fix he said سنان (teeth) instead of سنين (years). She asked 'What's سنان?' and recast it as سنين. Her chat note 'snaan = teeth' shows she heard it, so it was not a speech-to-text error. Only the first two claims count; the third repeats C34.

C36.why: When asked for the whole sentence he said تلجات, the wrong past form. Amal recast it as تَلَّجَت and he repeated ثلّجت.

C37.why: This is the same 40:24 moment as C38. Amal's 'إيش يعني؟' and her redirect were about meaning: wind doesn't 'come a lot'. Her echo 'عجا' and his switch to the singular 'Aja' are a side detail, so C38 is the better record of this moment.

C39.why: Duplicate of C38: it describes the same moment, and Amal's correction comes from 40:45, not a separate mistake at 40:40.

C44.why: Medi offered رمل as a question ('Is it رمل؟') while looking for a word he didn't know. Amal told him that means sand, he said he didn't know, and then he found تراب himself.
